newsitem.title: FINLAND: MARKKA-EURO FIX SEEN NEAR ERM MIDPOINT - OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: MARKKA-EURO FIX SEEN NEAR ERM MIDPOINT - OFFICIAL.

text.p: The exchange rate at which the markka will be irrevocably fixed to Europe's euro currency is unlikely to differ much from the markka's central parity rate in ERM, a senior Finnish finance ministry official said.

"I would find it difficult for some country to prove that something has happened to the fundamentals which would require a significant deviation from the central parity rate," Rauno Niinimaki, the ministry's EMU project chief, said in the foreign ministry's Kauppapolitiikka newsletter received on Tuesday.
The markka's ERM central parity exchange rate is 3.04 per German mark.

Niinimaki said European Union finance ministers were likely to decide on the final exchange rates in advance and not at the last moment before the scheduled January 1, 1999 transfer to the third stage of economic and monetary union (EMU).

The EMU entry criterion requiring two years of exchange rate stability -- some say ERM-participation is mandatory -- had been agreed to avoid surprises ahead of the switch-over from national currencies to the euro, Niinimaki said.
He did not expect major foreign exchange market speculation between May 1998, when the countries joining EMU in the first group will finally be selected, and January 1999.
If speculation occurred, it would indicate that the markets were expecting some other final exchange rates than prevailing market rates, he said.

"If a currency has been nicely close to its central parity rate I would be really surprised if it would become subject to speculation," he said, adding that market volatility may arise if some currencies were way off their central parities in ERM.
Niinimaki said the concept 'irrevocably fixed' was important. "Investors must under no circumstances be given the impression that some country might walk off the playing field," he said.
